cells.tense: Right now you are moving toward something and giving its shape a voice.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: At the next fork, hold two ways forward as both real. Take one and move on it, leaving the other true and uncarried, with nothing owed to yourself as explanation.
cells.core:
You are moving toward something with a direction in hand, and you are giving that direction a voice. That is the good version: the goal sharpens as you say it, and saying it does not slow the walking. People around the work can see where it is headed.

What stays loose is that a plan and a hope can feel the same from inside. So at the next fork, keep two live readings of the way forward side by side. Take one and act. The other can remain true and uncarried; you do not have to settle it before you move. Discernment here is holding both without forcing them into one. What the walking teaches you is worth more than what deciding settles in advance.

cells.verb: Declaring the framework outward and claiming the ground for what comes next
cells.place: On the drive toward the goal, where direction is held through resistance

cells.tense: You are raising the frame for a goal that will not arrive on a schedule you can write.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Take the part of the plan you have gone over most and follow it slowly to where your actual knowing stops. Halt there deliberately, not from tiredness.
cells.core:
A goal sits ahead and you are raising its frame already, building it for a walk that has not started. The structure is sound. It is also being built past the point where more building helps, because the road keeps rewriting the plan and you keep rewriting the plan to stay ahead of it.

Depth is what this needs, not more scaffolding. Take the part of the plan you have gone over most and follow it, slowly, until you hit what you do not know yet. That edge is real information, not failure. Stop there on purpose. A frame is not finished by being airtight; it is finished when it can hold a step you have not taken. Let the road hand you the next beam.

cells.tense: The goal you set going is behind you now, and you are still standing at its door.
cells.act: return to the work daily until it is profound
cells.ask: Do today's piece of the work you already started — one reachable step. Come back tomorrow and do that again, no finish line attached.
cells.core:
You set something moving once, and the direction is still on the books while you wait outside it. Not lazy, not confused. The structure you declared did not get picked back up, and the waiting has quietly become the posture. The urgency that started it is gone, and nothing new has taken its place.

The current comes back through the build itself, not through a bigger reason to want it. So do today's piece of the thing you already started — not the whole frame, one reachable step. Then come back tomorrow and do that again. Mastery here is made by returning to the work, not by waiting for the feeling that launched it. You do not need to want it first; the daily return carries its own pull.

cells.tense: The structure in this push is running, and the one steering it is not claiming the wheel.
cells.act: take in the yield of what was transformed
cells.ask: Look at what this push has produced so far. Choose a result, skill, or thing that exists now and did not before, and put it in your own words by hand.
cells.core:
Something in this push has already borne fruit — meetings held, decisions landed, a direction that held through resistance — and the fruit is being taken in. But the one taking it is not saying so. Asked, you would call it the work running itself. The hands on it are yours and are not being counted as yours.

The end of a stretch is a fine time to take stock. What did this actually grow? Choose one thing the push produced — a result, a skill, an object that exists now and did not before — and put it in your own words by hand, plainly, no smallness in it. What you take in by your own hand becomes yours in a way a thing carried quietly does not. One line. That is the whole cost.
cells.sheetLine: The push grew something. Put your hand near it.
